title: Self-hosted Grafana health dashboard | Life Dashboard
description: The Life Dashboard stack is a self-hosted Docker Compose setup with Postgres and six Grafana dashboards for Health Connect, Apple Health and screen time data.
h1: A self-hosted Grafana dashboard for your health data
lead: The Life Dashboard stack is an open-source Docker Compose setup for both apps: a receiver that checks signatures, Postgres and six Grafana dashboards. It's for people who want their records in SQL rather than in Home Assistant.

highlights.title: Six dashboards
highlights.text: Overview, Activity, Sleep, Heart and body, Screen time, and Data and sync, provisioned in a Life Dashboard folder.

highlights.title: Try it without a phone
highlights.text: The demo profile posts 60 days of made-up data for two phones through the real receiver.

highlights.title: Every record in Postgres
highlights.text: One records table with a JSONB column holds all 33 Android types and 28 iPhone types without schema changes.

highlights.title: SQL views for your own queries
highlights.text: The dash schema turns raw records into days, nights, hours and apps in your time zone.

highlights.title: A receiver that checks signatures
highlights.text: It verifies the X-Signature HMAC, applies a repeated payload once, and removes the records the phone reports as deleted.

highlights.title: Android and iPhone side by side
highlights.text: Each phone gets its own label in the webhook URL and shows up as its own Phone in every dashboard.

sections.h2: Sleep, activity, heart and screen time in Grafana
sections.text: Every dashboard has a Phone picker and links to the other five that keep the time range. Each panel has an info icon that says where its figure comes from.

bullets.sub: How today and last night went, and this week against the four before it.
Steps by hour, workout minutes against the WHO guideline of 150, a hypnogram, bedtime and wake time.
Heart rate per hour, resting heart rate, HRV, SpO2, breathing rate and weight with its 7-day mean.
Minutes per app and per day, the last use before sleep, and when each phone last sent data.

sections.h2: No scores, and a gap where data is missing
sections.text: Nothing is colored as good or bad. Goals are dashed lines you can change at the top of a dashboard.

bullets.sub: Steps, distance and calories come from the phone's daily totals, so a walk recorded by phone and watch counts once.

bullets.main: Local days in your time zone
bullets.sub: A night belongs to the morning you wake up. Today is marked “so far” and left out of averages.
RMSSD from an Android watch and SDNN from an Apple Watch are different measures, so they're never mixed.
A missing day shows as a gap. The only red is a phone that sent nothing for 24 hours.

sections.h2: Your health data in Postgres, ready for your own queries
sections.text: The dash views hold one row per day, night, hour or app, with local days already worked out. Query them with psql or in a Grafana panel of your own.

bullets.sub: Steps per day, counted once, per phone.
Hours asleep, deep and REM per night.
grafana_ro can only read the records and views, and its queries stop after 30 seconds. The same role can serve your own AI over MCP.

requirements: Docker with Compose, on a machine your phone can reach on the same network or over a VPN. On each phone, Life Dashboard Companion for Android or for iPhone, pointed at the receiver's webhook URL on port 8080 with a label for that phone, and the same secret as WEBHOOK_SECRET. To reach the receiver from outside, put a reverse proxy with TLS in front of it. The stack is offered as a starting point you can change, not as a finished product. Set a WEBHOOK_SECRET: without one the receiver accepts unsigned payloads.

faq.q: Can I try it before I connect a phone?
faq.a: Yes, if you can run Docker. The demo profile starts the stack with 60 days of made-up data for two phones, under its own name and ports. The commands are under Run the stack. Without Docker, the screenshots on this page show the same dashboards.

faq.q: Can I put it on the internet?
faq.a: Put a reverse proxy with TLS in front of the receiver only, and allow request bodies of 32 MB. Keep Grafana on your own network or behind a VPN: anyone who can view a dashboard can read every health record through the data source. On your own network, change GRAFANA_PASSWORD and GRAFANA_DB_PASSWORD in .env before the first start: Grafana's admin password defaults to lifedash, and both Grafana and the receiver listen on every interface of the machine. The Postgres owner's password is fixed in docker-compose.yml; Postgres publishes no port, so only the receiver reaches it.

faq.q: Can I use it next to Home Assistant?
faq.a: Yes, as a second home for the data, with two things to know today. The app keeps one signing secret per tab, and pairing with Home Assistant sets it, so a stack with its own secret then refuses the payloads: run the stack without a secret or with the same one, or send one phone to each. And a payload counts as delivered once one destination takes it, so if the stack is down at that moment, it misses that payload.

faq.q: How do I back it up?
faq.a: One pg_dump line writes a dump, and one pg_restore line puts it into a fresh stack. Restart the receiver afterward so it rebuilds the views and the grafana_ro grants.

Yes. They're provisioned from grafana/dashboards/life-dashboard/, so Grafana won't save changes over them: use Save as for a copy, or edit the JSON file. Keep views of your own in the public schema, because the receiver rebuilds dash at every start.

Series sent per time window are stored, but only the heart rate panels read them, so leave Data Resolution on Every record. Days follow the stack's one time zone, and a backfill doesn't remove records the phone no longer has. The known gaps list the rest.

faq.q: I already run Grafana. Can I use mine?
faq.a: Yes. Run the receiver and Postgres from the stack, and in your own Grafana add a PostgreSQL data source for the stack's database with the read-only user grafana_ro and your GRAFANA_DB_PASSWORD. Then import the six dashboard files from grafana/dashboards/life-dashboard/ and pick that data source. grafana_ro can read the records, the buckets and the dash views, and nothing else.

commands.title: Try it with demo data
commands.code:
git clone https://github.com/owen282000/life-dashboard-stack
cd life-dashboard-stack
RECEIVER_PORT=18080 GRAFANA_PORT=13000 \
  docker compose -p lifedash-demo \
  --profile demo up -d --build
commands.after: Give it a minute, then open http://localhost:13000 and log in as admin with the demo password lifedash. For your own data: cp .env.example .env, set four values, then docker compose up -d --build; the quick start has the details.
